english: The sum of all real numbers $x$ satisfying the equation
hindi: को सन्तुष्ट करने वाली सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का योग ______ है।
solution: AM $\ge$ GM: $4^{\sin^2\pi x}+4^{\cos^2\pi x}\ge2\sqrt{4^{\sin^2\pi x+\cos^2\pi x}}=4$, equality iff $\sin^2\pi x=\cos^2\pi x=\frac12$
So both sides must equal $4$: $x=\frac34$, and then $\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{4}=\frac12$ holds
solution_full: Both terms on the left are positive, so by AM $\ge$ GM: $4^{\sin^2\pi x}+4^{\cos^2\pi x}\ge2\sqrt{4^{\sin^2\pi x}\cdot4^{\cos^2\pi x}}=2\sqrt{4^{1}}=4$.
Equality holds exactly when $4^{\sin^2\pi x}=4^{\cos^2\pi x}$, i.e. $\sin^2\pi x=\cos^2\pi x=\frac12$, i.e. $x=\frac14+\frac n2$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$.
The right side satisfies $4-|4x-3|\le4$, with equality exactly when $x=\frac34$.
Since left side $\ge4\ge$ right side, the equation holds only if both equal $4$: $x=\frac34$ and $x\in\left\{\frac14+\frac n2\right\}$.
$x=\frac34=\frac14+\frac12$ is of this form ($\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{4}=\frac12$), so $x=\frac34$ is the only solution.
The sum of all solutions is $0.75$.
originality_note: New: an exponential trigonometric sum bounded below by AM-GM (minimum 4 at sin^2 = 1/2) set against a V-shaped bound above (maximum 4 at x = 3/4); the two equality sets must meet, and they do at one point (way 5). Closest known: 2^{sin x} + 2^{cos x} minimum problems and sin x = x^2 + 1 type boundedness equations. Different because: the lower bound needs AM-GM on exponentials and the equality points must be matched with the vertex of |4x - 3|.
blueprint_concepts: Equations solvable only by boundedness (e.g. sin(x).cos(x) = 1)

concept_use.Equations solvable only by boundedness (: Left side >= 4 and right side <= 4, so both must equal 4; the equality conditions sin^2 pi x = 1/2 and x = 3/4 are then matched.

key_step: Bounding the left side below by 4 with AM-GM and the right side above by 4.
justification: Two standard bounds and an equality check; a familiar boundedness pattern applied in two short stages. One step above the single-bound item 2024-P2-Q10 (L1).
